source.title: Instances Need More Care: Rewriting Prompts for Instances with LLMs in the Loop Yields Better Zero-Shot Performance
source.authors: Saurabh Srivastava; Chengyue Huang; Weiguo Fan; Ziyu Yao

page_placements.theme: A weaker model's text inserted into a stronger model's inference (rewritten prompts, RL-trained instructions, critiques, short reasoning segments)

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites weak-to-strong generalization and suggests prompt rewriting by a weaker model may have oversight potential, but it does not test fine-tuning a strong model on labels from a weaker model or measure PGR.
record.gate_note: The weaker-model results use instance-level prompt rewriting: a meta LLM revises prompts for a task LLM. This is not weak-label fine-tuning. The related outcomes are recorded under fits_no_version; they do not test any listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The study uses a weaker LLM (GPT-3.5, Mistral-7B) to rewrite test prompts at inference time for a stronger task LLM (GPT-4, Mixtral). No strong model is fine-tuned on weak-model labels, and no PGR is measured. The authors draw the analogy to weak-to-strong supervision and cite Burns et al., but their results bear on prompt optimization, not on any version of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that instance-level prompt rewriting with the task LLM in the loop improves zero-shot performance. They report that GPT-3.5 rewriting for GPT-4 matches or sometimes beats GPT-4 rewriting for itself, and say this shows potential for oversight. They do not frame it as a test of weak-label fine-tuning.
record.recipe_differences: The original claim concerns fine-tuning a strong model on weak-model labels and measuring PGR. This paper rewrites each test prompt using a meta LLM and evaluates zero-shot task performance; it does not fine-tune the task model.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by dataset and meta/task LLM pairing. On MATH, GPT-3.5 as GPT-4's meta LLM is slightly worse than GPT-4 as meta LLM; Table 4 also reports different scores for Mistral versus Mixtral as meta LLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: A weaker LLM used as a prompt-rewriting meta LLM improves a stronger task LLM's zero-shot performance over the stronger model's own zero-shot baseline. Examples: GPT-3.5 rewriting for GPT-4 (Figure 2); Mistral-7B rewriting for Mixtral, average 64.1 vs 49.8 (Table 4). Gains are large on ToxicChats and small on StrategyQA, MATH and MMLU (PM).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time weak-to-strong oversight via prompt rewriting: a weaker LLM rewriting prompts can improve a stronger LLM's zero-shot task performance.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: No direct evidence on the claim's weak-label fine-tuning intervention or PGR. The Figure 2 values for GPT-3.5 meta/GPT-4 task are not numerically available in the supplied text, and the reported results give no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results on weak-model prompt rewriting for a stronger task model were extracted beyond the GPT-3.5-to-GPT-4 outcomes in Figure 2 and the Mistral-to-Mixtral outcomes in Table 4. Other experiments do not report the related weaker-meta/stronger-task pairing or do not identify it as such.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning of a strong student on weak labels; no weak-supervisor baseline; no PGR.
No weak-to-strong training methods are compared.
No PGR dependence on size, task or representations.
No weak-to-strong failure modes. The meta LLM misjudging outputs (e.g. LastLetterConcat) concerns prompt rewriting, not weak-label training.

record.verdict_notes: The connection to weak-to-strong is only by analogy and citation (Burns et al., 2023). The stronger model's own zero-shot performance serves as the reference, and the weak model's standalone performance on the task is not compared, so PGR cannot even be approximated. The row states were changed from observed/partial to cannot_determine, since they cannot bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning of a strong student on weak-model labels; no comparison with the weak supervisor as a labeler; no PGR measurement.
The compared methods change prompts or refine outputs, not the weak-label fine-tuning methods named in this version.
The paper varies LLMs and tasks for prompt rewriting but does not measure PGR, weak-label fine-tuning, or representations as predictors.
No weak-label fine-tuning failure modes, distribution-shift PGR, or error-overlap analysis is tested.
No theoretical conditions for a student to beat a supervisor are analyzed.
No vision weak-label fine-tuning experiment is reported.

relation.reason: The introduction cites Burns et al. and discusses weaker models supervising stronger ones; the experiments and conclusion concern prompt rewriting and potential oversight.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates inference-time prompt rewriting, without fine-tuning a stronger student on weak-model labels or measuring PGR; it tests none of the listed claim versions.

source_check.notes: Table 4 gives averages of 64.129 and 49.843, correctly rounded in the statement. Metric descriptions are underspecified: §3.1 and Appendix A.1 identify standard metrics, including accuracy for StrategyQA/MATH and manual evaluation for ToxicChats; the supplied text is v4 dated 11 June 2024.
